newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Bel-20 index seen testing 2070 support.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Bel-20 index seen testing 2070 support.

text.p: Belgian shares closed lower on Monday as investors, made nervous by the Dow Jones' losses last week, continued to take profits on the rally of the past 12 months.
The Bel-20 index .BFX ended 18.18 points or 0.86 percent lower at 2,096.34, holding above the 2,070 support which has been tested twice since the correction started in mid-March.

"As long as the 2,070 support holds we are alright, but if it is broken, we can easily fall another 100 points," said KB Securities trader Pieter Hofman. "I do not rule out a break of that level this week," he added.
Much will depend on the Dow Jones, which was 0.3 percent lower at 6,370 in early U.S. trade.
"We could be heading for a rocky week," one trader said.
Insurer Fortis AG was the most active share, with more than 36,000 stocks traded for a 1.8 percent loss at 5,840 francs.

AG, along with Generale Bank, is no longer considered a strategic holding in the new French Suez-Lyonnaise group, the group's future new chairman Gerard Mestrallet told a newspaper this morning. Generale Bank was down 1.1 percent at 13,150 francs.
One dealer said that Fortis' fall was not due to Mestrallet's comments but to traders unwinding long positions.

Electrafina, a holding company belonging to Belgian businessman Albert Frere, rose 0.7 percent to 3,440 franc following news that Frere wanted to raise his stake in the merged group to about 8.3 percent from the current 5.3 percent.
